raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Every PR that runs full CI pays for two extra launches of the default Python server in `test_openai_server.py`, on CUDA (`base-b-test-1-gpu-small`) and AMD. Removing them saved 102 s of whole-file time on B200 when run the way CI runs it (382 s to 280 s), and 104 s, 146 s, and 52 s in other run pairs on a shared node. No CI runner was measured.

The saving is small. If a CI runner saves about 100 s, that is about 1% of `base-b-test-1-gpu-small` and about 0.1% of the 80,000-114,000 s CI total.

The OpenAI/Anthropic, Responses, and Score groups launch identical servers. The two extra launches took 93-114 s together, and the cases on the shared server took about 20 s.

No open PR I found shares these launches, and #44337 and #29810 only add other tests to this file.

## Modifications

The three groups become mixins on one `TestOpenAIServer` fixture. Launch arguments, other fixtures, CI registration, and remaining requests and assertions do not change.

The Responses `test_regex`, `test_response_prefill`, and `test_model_list` send the same request bytes as the OpenAI tests with those names, so this PR removes them. The Responses `test_penalty` calls `/v1/responses`, so it stays as `test_responses_penalty`.

## Accuracy Tests

`6118eda345` and `700318150f` are commits from before I squashed this branch onto main `7b88f09239`. The squash kept the same diff, and I did not repeat these runs on it. On the squashed commit, only pre-commit ran.

On B200s in the CI environment, I ran the whole file, including the Rust classes, on main 582168dd7c, head 6118eda345 (the fixture change), and head 700318150f (the removal). No case failed. With retries off, `TestOpenAIServer` at 700318150f ran reversed, shuffled, and twice in a row without failures.

No case reads another case's response ID or asserts on cached tokens, and the default server stores no Responses records.

Sharing one server couples these groups, but a crash already aborts the file: a SIGKILL with CI retries gave exit 137 on main and head 700318150f.

I did not run AMD, the small GPU runner, or GitHub CI (this draft has no `run-ci`). `est_time` stays unchanged: weekly-update-est-time.yml refreshes the CUDA value, and no AMD run measured this change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

| Work per complete file run | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Default Python server launches | 3 | 1 |
| Whole file on B200, run the way CI runs it (`-f`, `SGLANG_IS_IN_CI=true`) | 382 s (merge base 43881a719e) | 280 s (head 6118eda345) |
| Whole file on B200, one run each | 667.5 s (main 582168dd7c) | 563.5 s (main plus the fixture change, head 6118eda345) |
| The same runs without a slow first Rust launch of about 312 s, mostly cargo builds of the Rust extensions | about 355 s | about 251 s |
| Whole file on B200, two more run pairs | 440.2 s, 320.7 s (main ba1ed00dfe) | 294.3 s, 268.2 s (head 6118eda345 merged with that main) |
| Test removal only, one run, without its first Rust launch | about 251 s (head 6118eda345) | about 229 s (head 700318150f, 391 s with a first Rust launch of about 162 s). The removed tests took about 0.1 s together, so the removal does not explain that gap. |
| Whole file on the small GPU runner | 343-362 s since 2026-10-26 [archived](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang-ci-stats/tree/main/runs) | Not measured |

The B200 runs shared a node with different load per pair, so each difference is approximate.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
